name: scale_input_output_bias
hypothesis: Weaker main engine needs earlier and stronger main thrust. Scaling height up and vertical velocity magnitude up makes the network think it's higher and falling faster, prompting earlier main engine activation. Boosting the main engine logit and bias further encourages its use.

name: scale_input_output_bias2
hypothesis: Further increase perceived height and falling speed to trigger even earlier main thrust, and boost main engine logit and bias more strongly to compensate for the weaker engine. This should improve landing precision under weak_main without hurting nominal performance.

name: aggressive_input_main_scaling
hypothesis: Further amplify perceived height (×2) and falling speed (vertical velocity ×2) and also increase horizontal velocity scaling (×1.5) so the policy triggers main thrust earlier under weak_main. Reduce side‑engine influence by scaling their logits down (×0.8) and adding a small negative bias, while strongly boosting the main‑engine logit (×2.5) and adding a positive bias (0.4). Slightly amplify the second hidden layer (×1.2) to increase overall signal strength. This should raise goal_success_rate under weak_main without dropping nominal success below the 5% loss threshold.

name: height_vel_main_boost
hypothesis: Increase perceived height (×2.5) and falling speed (vertical velocity ×2.0) so the policy thinks it is higher and falling faster, prompting earlier main‑engine firing under weak_main. Boost the main‑engine logit (×2.5) and add a positive bias (0.4) to compensate for the reduced thrust. Keep other inputs unchanged to preserve nominal behavior.

name: height_vel_main_boost_more
hypothesis: Amplify perceived height (×3.0) and falling speed (vertical velocity ×2.5) and also increase horizontal velocity scaling (×1.5) so the policy thinks it is higher and descending faster, prompting much earlier main thrust. Downscale side‑engine logits (×0.7) and add a negative bias to discourage unnecessary side thrust. Strongly boost the main‑engine logit (×3.0) and add a large positive bias (+0.5) to compensate for the weaker engine. Slightly amplify the second hidden layer (×1.2) to increase overall signal strength while keeping nominal behavior stable.
